transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-06-08
- Start: 16:00 PDT
- Duration: 42 minutes
- Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Dana Liu (Redwood SE), Michael Chen (CTO, Rivermark), Aisha Gomez (Lead ML Eng), Jordan Hayes (PM)

Summary: quick hosted api demo covering chat and text generation basics. streaming, params, and retry semantics. customer asked about latency vs cost and security concerns.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samir: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm Samir from Redwood Inference, we also have Dana, our solutions eng, hi Dana.
[00:06] Dana: hi all, quick agenda - show hosted API, streaming demo, talk params (temp/top_p/max_tokens), how retries work, and then Q&A.
[00:16] Michael: sounds good, we've been evaluating a couple options, mostly interested in throughput for low-latency chat and safety/compliance.
[00:24] Samir: great - can you give us quick context on your stack and goals?
[00:30] Aisha: yeah, we're building an assistant inside our B2B app, typical traffic spikes, avg session is 3-4 messages, target p95 latency under 300ms for 512 tokens if possible. cost is a factor too - we want to keep per-user cost below a threshold.
[00:44] Jordan: timeline - pilot in 6 weeks, then determine dedicated or hosted. stakeholders are infra, security, and product.
[00:51] Dana: ok that helps. quick note - hosted API supports streaming so you can render tok by tok, and we have both streaming and chunked modes. i'll demo.
[01:05] Dana: (starts live demo) i'm calling the /v1/chat/completions endpoint, with model redwood-llm-v1, streaming enabled, and we stream tokens as they come. note, some SDKs show the event stream, sometimes transcribed as SSE.
[01:32] Michael: nice, how's retry handled if we see transient errors? we need idempotency for repeated requests.
[01:38] Samir: good q - default behavior: client should retry on 5xx and certain 429s with exponential backoff; we provide idempotency key header so repeated identical requests can be de-duped server-side. there is also a configurable retry_policy on dedicated plans.
[01:58] Aisha: does idempotency key work with streaming responses?
[02:03] Dana: yes, the key ties to the request; if the stream dies mid response we either resume (in some clients) or re-run based on idempotency semantics - there are tradeoffs, of course. in general we encourage short-lived streaming with caching of prefixes if you need lower cost.
[02:25] Jordan: you mentioned prefix caching earlier? how does that work?
[02:30] Dana: KV cache - it's basically prefix caching of previously generated tokens or context; reduces compute by avoiding re-computation of earlier tokens. it's automatic for repeated sessions if you provide conversation ids. sometimes our docs show k v cache as K V cache, devs misread that.
[02:49] Michael: on latency - do you have benchmarks vs other providers? we saw public numbers but want to run our prompts.
[02:56] Samir: totally, we can run a benchmark w your prompt set. we'll provision a small set of requests and measure p50/p95 on our hosted infra; for longer-term heavy workloads we recommend Dedicated.
[03:10] Aisha: what about batching? we can't sacrifice latency for throughput - how do batching and cost savings interplay?
[03:17] Dana: Redwood uses continuous batching - smallish windows to batch similar sequences; on hosted the default is conservative to preserve latency. you can tune batching vs throughput at deploy time on Dedicated or via request hints. batching reduces per-token cost, but increases latency slightly depending on traffic shape.
[03:36] Michael: security questions - SOC2, encryption keys, and data residency. we are in healthcare space so audits matter.
[03:43] Dana: we are SOC 2 Type II, yes, and we integrate with customer KMS for Private deployments; for hosted we offer customer-managed keys via cloud KMS in some regions, and audit logs in the console. we'll send the security pack after the call.
[03:59] Jordan: do you support SSO / SAML for console?
[04:02] Samir: yes SSO/SAML and RBAC are supported.
[04:06] Aisha: what about retention - do you store prompts and outputs? can we opt out?
[04:11] Dana: hosted by default stores for short-term metrics unless you opt out; we have options to disable retention and to enable data deletion on a schedule. on Dedicated/Private you control retention. we'll include docs.
[04:25] Michael: any hard limits on streaming length or token limits?
[04:29] Dana: models have max context, and the API enforces model max tokens; for long-running streams we recommend chunking responses or streaming partial summaries.
[04:40] Jordan: pricing - how do you charge for streaming? token-based?
[04:43] Samir: per-token billing still applies; streaming is just a delivery method. we bill input+output tokens; we also have reserved capacity pricing for Dedicated that changes unit economics.
[04:56] Aisha: curious about model variants - if we need smaller models for latency, are fallbacks automatic?
[05:01] Dana: smart routing can fallback to compatible variants to maintain SLOs; you can pin versions or allow automatic fallback to e.g. quantized models. note, some model names get auto-corrected in transcriptions - we saw 'Redwood Dedicate' in previous notes, it's 'Redwood Dedicated'.
[05:20] Michael: ok great. last q - client-side retries creating duplicate charges?
[05:26] Samir: idempotency keys handle dedupe; billing only counts completed successful responses. partial streams aborted mid-run shouldn't be billed for full output - we have internal heuristics. we can share specifics in the benchmark doc.
[05:40] Dana: demo wrap-up - i showed sample curl and JS SDK snippets: streaming with eventsource, setting temperature/top_p, max_tokens, stop sequences, and also a retry header: X-Idempotency-Key.
[05:58] Jordan: looks good, would like us to see cost estimates for our expected volume.
[06:03] Samir: action items - i'll email pricing + quickstart, Dana will share SOC2 + KMS notes, and we'll schedule a bench run with Aisha.
[06:10] Michael: perfect, thanks both.
